review_notes: I read the whole target file, the parent file IdealAdicRestricted.lean (definitions of adicReduction, polynomialToRestricted, the simp lemmas coeff_adicReduction and adicReduction_polynomial), and the test file for this module. The existing simp set (restrictAlongIdeal_coe, _refl, _polynomial, coeff_reductionAtLargerIdeal, reductionAtLargerIdeal_polynomial) looks confluent and well oriented. I saw no loops or competing rules. The findings are about missing simp lemmas at the level of whole ring-hom or polynomial values. I did not run Lean, so I have no evidence of simp behaviour. The claim that simp cannot currently close these goals comes from reading the simp set, not from an experiment. Whether the new lemmas should be simp is a judgment call, though the orientations are clearly shrinking.

findings.excerpt:
reductionAtLargerIdeal J K hJK (restrictAlongIdeal I J hIJ f) =
      reductionAtLargerIdeal I K (hIJ.trans hJK) f
findings.problem: This lemma has the shape of a normalising rewrite. It removes one `restrictAlongIdeal` and shrinks the term, so the right side is strictly simpler. Yet it is not `@[simp]`, while its siblings `restrictAlongIdeal_polynomial`, `reductionAtLargerIdeal_polynomial` and `coeff_reductionAtLargerIdeal` are. Simp can only reach the identity after taking `.coeff d`. At the polynomial level (`reductionAtLargerIdeal J K _ (restrictAlongIdeal I J _ f)`) it has no rule, and `restrictAlongIdeal_coe` only fires under a coercion. The test file has to invoke it by name with `rw` to do exactly this step.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`. The right side contains only the proof `hIJ.trans hJK`, which is irrelevant to matching, and no new ideals are introduced. The LHS ideals I, J, K are all determined by the arguments, so there is no unification problem. Optionally also mark `reductionAtLargerIdeal_map` (lines 136–143) `@[simp]` in the same pass. Its right side is a single reduction and its left side is a `map` of a reduction, so it is also shrinking. Check that the two do not compete with `coeff_reductionAtLargerIdeal`; they should agree on coefficients.
findings.benefit: Nested change-of-ideal expressions normalise to a single `reductionAtLargerIdeal` under `simp`. Callers no longer need manual `rw` chains like the one in the test file.

evidence.excerpt:
restrictAlongIdeal I J hIJ (polynomialToRestricted I p) =
      polynomialToRestricted J p

findings.excerpt:
(restrictAlongIdeal (σ := σ) J K hJK).comp (restrictAlongIdeal I J hIJ) =
      restrictAlongIdeal I K (hIJ.trans hJK)
findings.problem: Composition of inclusions is stated only as an equation of bundled `RingHom.comp`s, and it is not simp. The simp normal form for elements is the applied form `restrictAlongIdeal J K _ (restrictAlongIdeal I J _ f) = restrictAlongIdeal I K _ f`. Simp cannot derive this from the comp lemma, because `RingHom.comp_apply` is not used backwards. It is only handled when wrapped in a coercion by `restrictAlongIdeal_coe`. A term of type `adicallyRestrictedSubring K` that is not coerced stays as a nested double inclusion. The file already has `restrictAlongIdeal_refl` as simp, so the groupoid-like API is only half covered.
findings.proposed_change: Add an applied lemma `restrictAlongIdeal_apply_apply` (name suggestion) stating `restrictAlongIdeal J K hJK (restrictAlongIdeal I J hIJ f) = restrictAlongIdeal I K (hIJ.trans hJK) f` and mark it `@[simp]`. Prove it by `Subtype.ext` and `simp only [restrictAlongIdeal_coe]`, or from `restrictAlongIdeal_trans` with `RingHom.congr_fun`. Optionally keep the comp form as a non-simp lemma, or mark it `@[simp]` too, since the comp pattern is a different syntactic form.
findings.benefit: Chains of ideal enlargements collapse to one `restrictAlongIdeal` without manual `Subtype.ext` unfolding. This also lets `reductionAtLargerIdeal_restrictAlongIdeal` and the `_polynomial` lemmas fire after such collapses.

(restrictAlongIdeal I J hIJ f : MvPowerSeries σ R) = f

findings.excerpt:
reductionAtLargerIdeal I J hIJ f = 0 ↔
      ∀ d, coeff d (f : MvPowerSeries σ R) ∈ J
findings.problem: The only simp lemma that characterises vanishing is the coefficient lemma `coeff_reductionAtLargerIdeal`. A goal or hypothesis of the form `reductionAtLargerIdeal I J h f = 0` is not rewritten, because simp has no equation rule for `= 0` at this level. The proof of this iff itself needs `congrArg`/`ext` and a two-direction `simpa only` with `Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem`. In the test file the same iff is invoked explicitly with `.mpr`, which shows that downstream users do not get this from `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Consider tagging `reductionAtLargerIdeal_eq_zero_iff` with `@[simp]`. The direction is sound: the right side is a membership statement with no `reductionAtLargerIdeal`, and the iff cannot loop. A possible drawback is that it unfolds an equation into a universally quantified statement, which is less convenient for some uses. If so, keep it unmarked and say so in the docstring. The lemma is best-effort and optional.
findings.benefit: Vanishing of a larger-ideal reduction would normalise to the coefficientwise membership condition, which is the notion the rest of the API reasons about.
